tasks.short: Weigh letters and parcels, determine postage, and record the required service and charge.

steps.what: Place items on scales and measure dimensions where required.
Look up postage using weight, dimensions, destination, and requested service.
Copy the service and charge into the dispatch log.

tasks.design: Configure rate calculation in the {PARTNER_PORTAL}, using connected scales where supported and manual measurements otherwise. A small integration writes quotes and dispatch records to the {WORKFLOW}, removing the separate {SPREADSHEET} log; postage purchase remains a separate dispatch action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical handling remains necessary. Disconnected scales, rate tables, and dispatch logs made small integrations difficult to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing rate calculators and device connections handle the rules. AI-assisted coding can shorten implementation of the remaining connector without changing the physical work.
tasks.still_hard: Irregular parcels, dimensional charging, unsupported scales, and changing service restrictions. Software alone cannot move items onto scales.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise awkward packaging and clarify whether urgency, cost, or proof of delivery matters most.

ambition.what: Weekly review of avoidable premium postage

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time looking up rates and copying charges, while physical weighing remains. Dispatch records support weekly service recommendations; spending authority does not automatically change.

reach.task: Compare postage services against delivery requirements.
reach.learn: Dimensional pricing, service restrictions, and cost comparisons.

evidence.claim: Postage calculations follow structured weight, dimension, destination, and service rules; physical measurement remains necessary.
The proposed integration and time reductions are design estimates, not documented outcomes for this workplace.

assumptions: Routine postage is calculated through a carrier portal, with a separate dispatch log.
The portal supports configured rate calculation without a model.
Build ranges cover one dispatch station and existing equipment, excluding hardware procurement.
Time shares are estimates for this task, not shares of the whole job.
unknowns: Scale connectivity and portal integration access.
Whether a separate dispatch log exists or logging is already automatic.
Current rate contracts, parcel mix, and service restrictions.
Required access approvals and employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Can existing configuration capture measurements and export quotes without custom code?
Which parcel types require manual measurement or service selection?
new_work: Resolve missing measurements and failed record transfers.
Check sample quotes after rate changes.
Restrict address access and maintain retention settings under GDPR.

tasks.short: Prepare letter batches, fold and insert documents, and check envelope contents.

steps.what: Arrange printed letters, enclosures, and envelopes into matching batches.
Fold and insert documents by hand or with a folder inserter.
Check enclosure matches, address visibility, and batch counts before sealing.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator in the {WORKFLOW} creates batch sheets from approved mailing instructions in the {DOCS}. Standard batch sizes and saved settings simplify use of the existing folder inserter, while the clerk loads materials, handles unusual enclosures, and approves the contents check.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on physical materials and suitable machinery. Mixed formats and inconsistent batch instructions reduce the value of standard machine settings.
tasks.enabler_now: Small generators can produce consistent batch sheets and counts cheaply. Existing machinery may already support reusable settings; no model breakthrough is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Thin paper, unusual enclosures, jams, and confidential documents require physical handling. Meaningful further savings may require equipment investment rather than software.
tasks.human_edge: Detect mismatched contents and handle fragile or unusual materials before confidential information reaches the wrong recipient.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends slightly less time arranging batches and resetting machinery. Physical insertion and checking remain substantial, and decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare consistent mailing instructions and enclosure lists.
reach.learn: Print ordering, envelope specifications, and recipient-to-enclosure matching.

evidence.claim: Folder inserters can mechanise routine folding and insertion but still require loading, setup, and exception handling.
Batch sheets and reusable machine settings can reduce preparation work; the proposed reductions require local validation.

assumptions: The mailroom already has a folder inserter for standard batches.
Mailing content and recipient lists have been approved before this task.
The target retains physical mail where required or requested; channel migration belongs upstream.
Build ranges exclude purchasing machinery and changing the upstream document-generation system.
Without suitable machinery, physical insertion time remains close to today's.
unknowns: Existing machine capabilities, condition, and supported formats.
Batch volumes and the share requiring hand insertion.
Availability of reliable mailing instructions and enclosure counts.
Applicable employee consultation and equipment training requirements under national rules.
research_questions: Can simpler print ordering remove batch rearrangement before adding software?
Do existing machine controls provide useful double-feed or count checks?
new_work: Maintain batch templates and saved machine settings.
Reconcile spoiled items and reprints against batch counts.
Train staff on jams and unusual materials.
Control access to recipient lists and dispose of spoiled prints securely.

tasks.short: Separate restricted incoming mail, open permitted envelopes, and seal prepared outgoing mail.

steps.what: Separate incoming envelopes marked personal, confidential, or requiring special handling.
Open permitted envelopes by hand or opener, checking for retained contents.
Seal checked outgoing envelopes by hand or with a sealing machine.

tasks.design: Keep approved opening rules in the {DOCS} and use consistent physical trays for restricted and permitted mail. Standardise envelope stock and configure existing sealing equipment for routine outgoing batches; the clerk retains opening decisions and physical handling.
tasks.previous_blocker: Opening and sealing are physical operations. Confidential markings, mixed envelope sizes, and fragile contents limit unattended processing.
tasks.enabler_now: Clearer rules, standard materials, and existing equipment settings offer modest gains now. AI coding adds little to the physical operation itself.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous confidentiality markings, damaged envelopes, concealed enclosures, and equipment jams. Scanning after opening does not eliminate opening.
tasks.human_edge: Respect handling restrictions and recognise when an envelope should remain unopened or receive special treatment.
tasks.altitude: The week changes little: the clerk still opens and seals physical mail. Standard batches reduce some handling, with no additional decision rights.

reach.task: Preserve original documents and envelope evidence when required.
reach.learn: Document integrity, retention categories, and restricted access procedures.

evidence.claim: Physical opening and sealing require manual handling or dedicated equipment; software alone does not perform them.
PostNL offers business-post scanning and form digitisation, which addresses downstream processing rather than eliminating envelope opening.

assumptions: Incoming opening and outgoing sealing are separate daily streams, not consecutive actions on the same envelope.
Existing opening and sealing equipment remains in use.
Outgoing contents have already passed the separate insertion check.
Savings depend on standard materials and equipment setup, not new robotics.
Build ranges exclude new equipment procurement.
unknowns: Which categories the mailroom is authorised to open.
Envelope mix and existing equipment capabilities.
Required consultation, safety instruction, and access changes under national rules.
research_questions: Can envelope standardisation reduce sealing exceptions without changing correspondence requirements?
Which restricted-mail categories need clearer written instructions?
new_work: Keep opening rules current with authorised departments.
Handle damaged contents and failed seals.
Review handling procedures under GDPR and applicable national rules.

tasks.short: Inspect delivered mail containers, reconcile manifests, record acceptance, and notify recipients or report discrepancies.

steps.what: Inspect delivered containers, count units, and note visible damage or broken seals.
Compare container identifiers and counts with the delivery manifest and expected deliveries.
Sign for receipt and record any reservations about count or condition.
Notify recipients of arrivals and contact the contractor about delivery discrepancies.

tasks.design: A receipt app in the {WORKFLOW} captures scanned identifiers, counts, and condition observations, then compares them with structured manifests from the {PARTNER_PORTAL}. The clerk confirms physical receipt and reservations before signing; approved receipt events generate notices through the {EMAIL}, with external discrepancy notices checked before sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper manifests, inconsistent identifiers, and physical condition checks prevent fully automatic acceptance. Receipt evidence and follow-up often sit in separate paper records and mailboxes.
tasks.enabler_now: Barcode capture, structured manifests, simple matching rules, and templated notices need no model. AI-assisted coding can make a small receipt app and connector cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden damage, disputed counts, missing labels, and contractors without digital manifests. A clean data match cannot establish physical condition.
tasks.human_edge: Inspect the delivery, make factual reservations, and resolve disagreements with the driver without overstating what was checked.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time comparing identifiers and writing notices, while retaining physical acceptance decisions. Receipt history supports better follow-up; authority to settle contractor claims does not change.

reach.task: Maintain delivery evidence for shortages and damage claims.
reach.learn: Chain of custody, factual reservations, and the difference between receipt and contents verification.

reach.task: Improve delivery access windows and internal collection arrangements.
reach.learn: Aggregate arrival patterns and collection delays without measuring individual worker speed.

evidence.claim: Barcode capture, deterministic manifest matching, and templated notices can support receiving without automating physical inspection.
The proposed receipt workflow and remaining-time estimates are not documented customer outcomes.
In the Netherlands, the cited works-council provision is relevant to systems monitoring employee performance; national rules vary.

assumptions: Deliveries usually include a manifest and identifiable containers.
The first release uses structured manifests or manual count entry; free-text extraction is unnecessary.
Receipt confirmation does not certify unseen contents.
External discrepancy notices require clerk approval; routine internal arrival notices can follow approved receipt records.
Build ranges cover one receiving point and one manifest connection, excluding equipment procurement.
unknowns: Manifest formats, barcode coverage, and partner access permissions.
Who may sign, refuse delivery, or record reservations.
Recipient directory quality and current notification practices.
Evidence retention periods and contractor dispute procedures.
Employee consultation requirements under national rules and whether individual activity monitoring is intended.
research_questions: Can contractors provide structured manifests before arrival?
Which identifier reliably links a container, manifest, and receipt?
Can aggregate service measures answer operational questions without individual worker monitoring?
new_work: Resolve unmatched identifiers and incomplete manifests.
Maintain recipient mappings and notice templates.
Check failed notices and duplicate receipts.
Manage receipt evidence access and retention under GDPR.
Review EU AI Act obligations if a model-based component is later introduced.
Consult employees under applicable national rules when changing work organisation or introducing monitoring.

role.altitude: The role remains physical: receiving, inspecting, opening, loading, and handling exceptions. Deterministic tools reduce rate lookup, duplicate records, and routine correspondence; they do not automatically expand spending or claims authority.
reach: Support logistics analysis with reliable dispatch costs and service requirements.
Support shipping and receiving with traceable receipt evidence.
Help facilities management improve delivery and collection arrangements.
Work with administrative assistants to standardise mailing batches.
skills_to_grow: Configure postage rules and machine settings.
Use barcode-based receipt records and reconcile exceptions.
Preserve delivery evidence and document factual reservations.
Apply confidentiality, access, and retention procedures.
Compare service costs and identify recurring physical bottlenecks.
role.ambitious_version: Run a dependable workplace mail service with tracked parcel arrivals and regular postage-service reviews. Better records support operational decisions, while people retain physical inspection and acceptance.

job.title: Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service
